comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Citigroup disclosed the successful dismissal of securities class action complaints in 2024. Goldman Sachs reported that the court granted the motion to dismiss the amended complaint in the Yatsen Holding litigation on July 22, 2024. Similarly, Citigroup disclosed that its motions to dismiss were granted in previous years (2019 and 2020) for related securities litigation, although a separate antitrust claim was reinstated; however, the C candidate c_2024_8_D693 specifically focuses on the securities litigation where the court granted dismissal without prejudice in March 2023, allowing plaintiffs to amend. A more direct comparison for 'dismissal' in 2024 is the Yatsen case. Looking at C's candidates, c_2024_8_D693 describes a dismissal granted without prejudice in 2023. The GS case is a dismissal granted in 2024. Both involve securities class actions where the underwriter/bank faced a motion to dismiss. The GS disclosure details a final dismissal of the amended complaint. The Citigroup disclosure details a dismissal without prejudice which led to an amended complaint. Both represent significant procedural victories or milestones in underwriting-related securities litigation, though the outcomes (final vs. without prejudice) and timing (2024 vs 2023) differ. Another C candidate, c_2024_8_D695, involves antitrust, not securities. Therefore, c_2024_8_D693 is the most comparable topic (Securities Litigation Dismissal).
